sections.html:
Mesa residents pay the Maricopa County Treasurer's Office, not City Hall. Valuation comes from the Maricopa County Assessor. Mesa doesn't assess or collect anything itself, yet its charge appears on the same statement as the county, school district, community college district and special districts.

Payment questions go to the Treasurer's customer service line, 602-506-8511. Value questions go to the Assessor, 602-506-3406. You can visit the Treasurer in person at 301 West Jefferson Street, Suite 100, Phoenix, between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.

sections.h2: The city's share of the bill
sections.html:
Mesa levies no primary property tax and does levy a secondary one. Under Arizona's two-part system, that secondary tax repays voter-approved general obligation bonds for libraries, parks and recreation, public safety and transportation. The rate held steady for the three most recent years in the table.

Fiscal yearTaxable valueCity rate per $100 of valueCity levy
2025/26$5.2 billion$0.8582$44.3 million
2024/25$4.9 billion$0.8582$42.0 million
2023/24$4.5 billion$0.8582$38.8 million
2022/23$4.2 billion$0.9157$38.8 million
2021/22$4.0 billion$1.1319$45.2 million

A median-value Mesa home paid $159 of city secondary levy in 2025/26. Some parcels also sit in a Community Facility District, where bonds financed property development and the cost is assessed to the owners. If you aren't sure whether your parcel is inside one, the Treasurer can tell you, and the answer changes your bill.

The city follows the county's schedule. Two installments are due, one on October 1 and one on March 1 (A.R.S. 42-18052), and each becomes delinquent at 5:00 p.m. on November 1 or May 1. Weekend and holiday cutoffs slide forward to the next business day, which gave the 2026 first half until 5 p.m. on Monday, November 2.

  • Pay all of the 2026 tax over $100 by December 31, 2026, and no interest applies.
  • Second-half money is due March 1, 2027.
  • May 1, 2027 lands on a Saturday, so lateness starts at 5:00 p.m. the next business day.
  • A bill of $100 or less is due whole on October 1 and goes late after December 31.

Interest on late tax is simple, 16% a year, counted from the delinquency date (A.R.S. 42-18053). Pay the full year by December 31, or have the delay traced to an office error, and it isn't charged. The Treasurer's calendar also schedules an advertising fee in January for delinquent taxes and an online lien auction in February.

Your petition goes to the Maricopa County Assessor, and the clock is 60 days from the mailing of the Notice of Value. The notice arrives between January 1 and March 1. A.R.S. 42-16051 sets that window and treats a postmark as filing. Give your own figure for full cash value and the method behind it, for example a comparable property or a recent sale.

Only full cash value and legal classification can be appealed. Tax is figured on limited value, which is held to 5% growth a year unless the house itself changes. Values lag the market: they rest on sales from two to three years earlier, so the value used for fiscal 2025/26 came from mid-2022 to mid-2023 sales.

If the Assessor's reply leaves you unsatisfied, the State Board of Equalization hears an appeal filed within 25 days. Court is the last step, in Superior Court's tax division or small claims, by December 15 of the notice year or 60 days after an administrative decision. Small claims suits are for owner-occupied homes and property under $2 million. A rental that isn't the owner's primary residence belongs in tax court.

sections.h2: Selling a Mesa home: what buyers ask
sections.html:
Mesa counted 504,258 residents in 2020 and is estimated at 513,656 for 2025. Mesa Public Schools covers most of the city. The southern part is served by Gilbert Public Schools, the Higley Unified School District and the Queen Creek Unified School District, and a thin western strip belongs to Tempe districts. Buyers who compare schools will want to know your district, and it also shapes the school share of your bill.

Center Street is the east-west dividing line, and address numbering differs from Phoenix's, so verify yours before it goes on a deed or listing. Home ages range widely: the city grew from 16,790 residents in 1950 to 63,049 in 1970 and passed 500,000 by 2020.

sections.h2: Changes that raise your assessed value
sections.html: A new room, a major addition or a switch in how the property is used can lift limited property value past the 5% cap. The Assessor then sends a Notice of Change, and you have 25 days to appeal to the State Board of Equalization. Save the permits for anything you built, since they show what was added and when. A buyer's agent may ask for them, and so might the Assessor.

Think of the county bill as a payoff figure. The tax lien for the year attached on January 1 (A.R.S. 42-17153) and outranks most other liens, state liens and liens for other years excepted. The Treasurer can quote what is owed through your closing date. Send that number to the title company, which pays it from your proceeds. Interest on a delinquent half has been running since it went late.

Recording is a separate step. The deed and the affidavit of property value required by A.R.S. 11-1133 go to the Maricopa County Recorder, at $30 per document. Title companies normally handle the payoff and the recording together.

A simple order of work: look up your parcel on the Treasurer's site to see if either half is open, request the payoff, send it to title, then read the settlement statement for a tax line that matches. If a cash buyer closes quickly, less interest builds on a late half, although the balance still comes out of the sale at closing.

After closing, mail addressed to you may still arrive. Forward any tax bill to the new owner, and keep your closing statement as proof of what was paid and when, in case a question comes up later about which half belonged to whom.

faqs.q: Does Mesa have its own property tax?
faqs.a: Only a secondary one. Mesa has no primary levy, and the secondary tax repays voter-approved bonds. The 2025/26 rate was $0.8582 per $100 of value, which was $159 for a median-value home.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Mesa property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Maricopa County Treasurer, who collects for Mesa along with the county, schools and special districts. You can pay on the Treasurer's website, by calling 602-506-8511, or at 301 West Jefferson Street, Suite 100, Phoenix.

faqs.q: When did the 2026 first-half Mesa property tax go delinquent?
faqs.a: At 5:00 p.m. on Monday, November 2, 2026, since November 1 was a Sunday. Pay the full year by December 31, 2026 to avoid interest. The second half is due March 1, 2027.

faqs.q: How long do I have to contest my Mesa property value?
faqs.a: Sixty days, counted from the day the Maricopa County Assessor mailed your Notice of Value. Use the Petition for Review of Real Property Valuation. If you appeal further, the State Board of Equalization wants it within 25 days of the Assessor's decision.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Mesa house that still owes property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. At closing the title company takes the lien amount out of your proceeds. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff dated to closing, because overdue amounts accrue 16% a year.
